quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When riding, jackets and pants should:

options.text: Fit loosely so wind can catch the fabric.
Fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.
Fit tightly so you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fit snugly so they don't flap in the wind.
questions.explanation: Jackets and pants should fit snugly enough that they don't flap in the wind, but loose enough that you can move freely.

questions.question: Before riding, a motorcycle operator should check the throttle. The throttle should:
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your clutch and throttle. The throttle should snap back when you let go, and the clutch should feel tight and smooth.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be made of leather or a similar durable material to provide maximum grip and protection.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcycle rider should:

options.text: Keep an adequate space cushion around your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep an adequate space cushion around your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always allow yourself enough space around your motorcycle to reduce collision risk. Keep this space when following other vehicles, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing lanes.

questions.question: After riding over an object on the road, you should:

options.text: Continue riding because the danger has passed.
Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
Stop to remove the object from the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and check your tires and rims for damage.
questions.explanation: After riding over an object on the road, pull off the road to check your tires and rims for damage before continuing. Also check that nothing is caught in the drive chain or belt.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They warn you about upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, you should ensure that it:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, yield to other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: Taking over-the-counter medication before riding:

options.text: Is usually fine because over-the-counter medications are not very strong.
May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: May affect your riding abilities and should be done with caution.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medications, can impair your ability to safely operate a motorcycle. Talk to your doctor about how a new medication may affect your riding.

questions.question: To get the most protection from your helmet, make sure it:
questions.explanation: Your helmet will protect you best if it meets safety standards, fits snugly around your entire head, and has no damage.

questions.question: When traveling at night, it is:

options.text: Easier to judge distances than it is during the day.
About as easy to judge distances as it is during the day.
More difficult to judge distances than it is during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult to judge distances than it is during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge how far away objects are at night. During the day, shadows and light help you see distance. At night, artificial lights may distort or hide these helpful clues.

questions.question: To reduce fatigue during a long ride, you should:
questions.explanation: Take frequent rest breaks to help reduce fatigue. Caffeine may make you feel alert at first, but you may crash when it wears off, which increases fatigue and danger. Dress warmly and use a windshield to protect yourself from wind and weather.

questions.question: The best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle is to:
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Most motorcycles made after 1978 turn on the headlight automatically when running. Check that your headlight works before every ride.

questions.question: Choose a lane position that:

options.text: Hides you from other road users.
Places you directly next to another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Pick a lane position that helps you avoid road hazards. Always keep safe space around your motorcycle.

questions.question: A flat front tire is especially dangerous because:

options.text: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
The front tire being flat will disable the front brake.
The front tire being flat will prevent you from accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front tire affects your steering, which also affects your balance.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering and balance. If steering feels heavy, you may have a flat front tire.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear brightly-colored, reflective clothing whenever you ride, day or night.

questions.question: The front brake:

options.text: Should only be used in an emergency.
Should be used with the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be used with the rear brake.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Only wear a jacket at night.
Only wear a jacket if it is cold outside.

questions.explanation: Always wear a sturdy jacket with long sleeves when riding, even in warm weather.

questions.question: As a rider, you can reduce your chances of an accident by:

options.text: Not using turn signals so you don't distract other drivers.

questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, make yourself visible, use clear signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, watch ahead for hazards, and be ready to react quickly.

questions.question: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. What do they mean?
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line means you cannot pass. A dashed white line means you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow-moving vehicles going under 25 mph. Examples include construction equipment, farm machinery, and horse-drawn vehicles.

questions.question: How can you tell your rear tire has suddenly gone flat?

options.text: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
A discharge of air can be seen.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back of your motorcycle is swaying from side to side.
questions.explanation: When a rear tire goes flat, the back of the motorcycle will jerk or sway side to side. If you feel this movement, stop and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a blind intersection?

options.text: Assume that other drivers will properly yield the right-of-way.
Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position to become more visible to other drivers.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, move to the lane position that makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather boots offer the best protection. They should be high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles.
